page: Amazon Web Services i2.8xlarge is a storage-optimized second-generation instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 cores running at 2.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. System resources include 244.0 GB of memory (7.62 GB per vCPU), 25 MB of L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. High-speed local disk capacity is provided via 6400 GB of NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results indicate steady multi-core computational throughput alongside high-capacity storage capability. PassMark CPU scoring reaches 29387.12, and stress-ng multi-core execution achieves 27789.21. Memory bandwidth testing demonstrates uncached read rates of 82.93 GB/sec and write rates of 37.47 GB/sec. However, single-core performance presents a limitation, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 534.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 20.36 GB/sec.

The instance delivers high resource density for IO-intensive processing, achieving 11.15 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database test scores of 12597.61. The high capacity of local NVMe SSD storage bundled with substantial RAM makes this platform cost-efficient for large analytical databases, data caching layers, and IOPS-heavy transactional workloads. Older CPU architecture limits its suitability for single-threaded tasks or intensive machine learning workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services i2.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs from 16 physical Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 cores operating at 2.5 GHz. It combines 244.0 GB of memory with 6400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network capability. Performance benchmarks show middle-tier multi-threaded capabilities, evidenced by a 27789.21 stress-ng multi-core score and 11.15 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core execution is constrained, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 534.0 and weak single-threaded gzip compression. The server provides strong resource density for data-heavy operations where local SSD capacity and memory capacity take priority over single-core clock efficiency. It is suitable for high-throughput database systems, NoSQL datastores, static web serving, and memory-intensive caching tiers.
